apps.name: Identity
apps.summary: Sign in once with an email code, a passkey or Google, and every OS app knows who you are. Someone new asks for access to the apps they need, with a note, and an admin approves.

surfaces.note: Sign-in, your account and access requests.

apps.name: Docs
apps.summary: A private reader for documentation repositories: read the Markdown, keep study notes on it, and turn a note into a GitHub issue in the repository that owns the document.

surfaces.note: For people an admin gave a Docs role.

apps.name: Flow
apps.summary: Build a workflow visually, start it from an OS event, a webhook or GitHub, and let people approve or reject a step before it goes on. Six connectors, an encrypted credential store, and drafts written by Claude from an issue, which never run by themselves.

surfaces.note: For people an admin gave a Flow role.

apps.name: Admin
apps.summary: Installed apps and their state, roles and grants, access requests, and one audit centre for sign-ins, access decisions and admin changes.

surfaces.note: For admins only, so it is not linked here.

apps.name: Notes
apps.summary: The smallest app that shows the contract end to end: a manifest, its own database, registering itself, sign-in through Identity, roles granted by an admin.

surfaces.note: Runs in the dev environment; not deployed.

apps.name: IGS-Pharma
apps.summary: Built with a Belgian pharmacy: a webshop for non-prescription products with a pharmacist in the loop, a back-office for the pharmacy team, and a free Android app. Its own code and domain, with the OS's look; the project page is served by the OS stack.

surfaces.note: The project, in Dutch, French, German and English, with the app's privacy pages.
Closed until launch: customers the pharmacy invites or approves see it already.
Browse, search, scan a pack and keep a list; orders go to the webshop. In internal testing.
Catalogue, prices, stock and recalls, orders, delivery and early access, behind a passkey.

apps.name: Breinhap
apps.tagline: Short study missions for secondary school
apps.summary: A study app for Flemish secondary-school students, designed with ADHD and AuDHD in mind: missions of 2 to 6 minutes, always in the same four steps.

surfaces.note: What the app is, in Dutch and English, with its privacy pages.
In a closed test before it opens to everyone.

shipped.title: Foundations
shipped.summary: The workspace, CI and the self-describing app contract: an app's manifest, its validator and JSON Schema, and the platform CLI that compiles manifests and checks that the core never imports an app.

shipped.title: Local dev environment
shipped.summary: One command starts the whole OS locally: Postgres, Redis, identity, core-api, a dev login stub with seeded users, and a dev gateway in front of every app.

shipped.title: Identity
shipped.summary: The OpenID Connect provider for id.asafarim.site, with sign-in delegated to Hub, plus its published container image and production deploy files.

shipped.title: Control plane
shipped.summary: core-api's registry, permission catalog and lifecycle; the app SDK and Notes, the first built-in app; the Admin console for apps, roles, grants and the audit log.

shipped.title: Event bus and bus auth
shipped.summary: NATS JetStream with CloudEvents, an outbox and relay, durable consumers with dedupe and dead letters, and per-app bus permissions checked by core-api when an app connects.

shipped.title: Event catalog
shipped.summary: Apps upload signed schemas for the events they publish, and the Admin console lists every event type with its publisher, subscribers and schema.

shipped.title: Remove an app
shipped.summary: The last lifecycle step: an admin removes an app, its grants and bus resources are cleaned up, and it can be installed again from scratch.

shipped.title: Health and status board
shipped.summary: core-api checks every active app's live and ready endpoints from its manifest, and the Admin console shows them on one Status page.

shipped.title: This page is live
shipped.summary: asafarim.site now serves the OS landing page from its own container, deployed on its own with one command and no identity. The placeholder page is gone.

shipped.title: Traces, request metrics and trace-id logs
shipped.summary: Every app's requests become OpenTelemetry traces and per-route rate, error and duration metrics, with only route patterns leaving the app, and its JSON log lines carry the trace id. One command starts a local collector.

shipped.title: Install an app from its image
shipped.summary: An app built in another repository is installed from its container image: its manifest travels as an image label and is validated, and one command runs it locally or writes its production compose file.

shipped.title: A private documentation reader
shipped.summary: docs.asafarim.site, the second built-in app: it renders documents from their source repository with contents and search, keeps study notes on a part of a document, and is open only to the people the OS grants it to.

shipped.title: Traces across apps
shipped.summary: One request stays one trace through the gateway, core-api and the event bus, and every app flushes its traces and metrics when it stops.

shipped.title: Backup and purge
shipped.summary: Removing an app first backs up its database. The database is dropped only after a retention window, and only if the backup is still there and unchanged. The CLI can remove, purge and list them.

shipped.title: Manifest review
shipped.summary: Every pull request gets an advisory check that compares an app's manifest with its code: unguarded routes, permissions never checked, and events without a schema or a handler, posted as one comment.

shipped.title: Email codes and passkeys
shipped.summary: id.asafarim.site signs people in with a one-time email code or a passkey, built in the OS with no outside provider, and an admin approves new connections.

shipped.title: Event search
shipped.summary: The Admin console's event catalog answers questions like "which app emits something when an order ships?" by searching event types, apps and schema descriptions.

shipped.title: Database time in every trace
shipped.summary: Queries from core-api, Notes and Docs show up in their request's trace with the operation and the database name only, never the SQL text or its values.

shipped.title: App switcher and account menu
shipped.summary: Every OS app has the same top bar: a switcher to each app you can open, and an account menu with your name and Sign out.

shipped.title: core-api and its own database
shipped.summary: core-api runs in production next to the OS's own Postgres on a private network, started by the deploy only once its encrypted settings are committed. A failed image pull is retried before the deploy gives up.

shipped.title: Down and recovered alerts
shipped.summary: core-api can send one message to a chat webhook when an app goes down and one when it recovers. It keeps the history on the Status page, and remembers what it already reported across a restart.

shipped.title: Scaffold a new app
shipped.summary: One command writes a new app with its manifest, sign-in, the OS top bar, a permission-checked example route, health endpoints, telemetry and a test. It passes manifest review with no findings.

shipped.title: Admin console in production
shipped.summary: The Admin console runs at admin.asafarim.site: admins manage apps, roles, grants and the audit log there.

shipped.title: The OS from the command line
shipped.summary: The platform CLI reads what the Admin console shows: the audit log, every app and its state, one app's permissions and roles, who holds which role, and the event catalog with its keyword search.

shipped.title: Backups checked on demand
shipped.summary: A removed app's backup can be verified at any time, from the command line or from the Admin console's Apps page, before its database is purged.

shipped.title: One look for every app
shipped.summary: One light and dark theme with a toggle in every header, data tables that fit a phone, a shared layout for the sign-in pages, and a link to the Admin console for admins.

shipped.title: Breinhap and IGS-Pharma
shipped.summary: The OS stack also serves the landing pages of two ventures built in their own repositories, breinhap.asafarim.site and igs.asafarim.site, linked from every OS navigation.

shipped.title: Privacy, cookies and terms
shipped.summary: Privacy, cookie and terms pages linked from every OS footer, and a sitemap, share preview and structured data for this page.

shipped.title: Continue with Google and access requests
shipped.summary: id.asafarim.site adds Continue with Google next to email codes and passkeys, with redesigned sign-in pages. A new person asks for access to the apps they need, with a note, and an admin approves.

shipped.title: An audit centre
shipped.summary: The Admin console shows sign-ins, access decisions and admin changes in one audit centre.

shipped.title: Flow, the workflow app
shipped.summary: flow.asafarim.site, the third built-in app: workflows that run on events, with approval steps a person approves or rejects. Its first workflow has the Docs app draft a GitHub issue and creates it once someone approves.

shipped.title: The event bus in production
shipped.summary: NATS joins the production stack, and core-api, Docs and Flow connect to it when it runs.

shipped.title: One sign-out everywhere
shipped.summary: An app's session ends when the identity session does, and signing out of an app also ends the id.asafarim.site session. A test fails if the two lifetimes drift apart.

shipped.title: A deeper manifest review
shipped.summary: Manifest review catches many more mismatches between an app's manifest and its code: secrets, config and permissions declared but never used or used but never declared; routes, health paths and launcher tiles nothing serves; events and schemas that don't line up; database gaps; and names or ports that clash. The CLI's README lists every finding, and a test keeps the list complete.

shipped.title: The workflow builder and connectors
shipped.summary: Flow gets a visual builder, a new workflow format and the engine that runs it, webhook and GitHub event triggers, six outbound connectors, and an encrypted credential store behind an allow-list of the hosts it may reach.

shipped.title: A new app switcher
shipped.summary: An icon-only app switcher in every app, one menu open at a time, and a launcher panel that a host page's styles can't break.

shipped.title: Workflow files and drafts from issues
shipped.summary: Workflows can be exported, printed and imported as files. Flow can also draft a workflow from a GitHub or GitLab issue with Claude: the draft never runs by itself, and every step that sends data out arrives unconfigured.

shipped.title: Flow, hardened
shipped.summary: Pause all stops work already in flight and fails closed. The public webhook endpoint answers unknown and forged calls the same way and limits floods per source, and credentials stay bound to their settings.

roadmap.summary: A read-only live demo of core-api, Admin and Notes, and TLS and operator mode for the event bus, now that it runs in production.

roadmap.title: Observability
roadmap.summary: Metrics, traces and logs in one place with dashboards, alerts on traces and metrics, and a public status board.

roadmap.title: AI assist
roadmap.summary: AI help where text matching can't see: drafting a new app's manifest, a deeper manifest review, semantic event search and a read-only copilot in the Admin console.

roadmap.title: Scheduled workflows
roadmap.summary: Workflows that start on a schedule, and new workflows that run as a dry run first.
